name: ClickHouse
summary: ClickHouse sells a fast open-source analytics database and cloud service used by more than 4,000 customers, including Anthropic, Meta and Capital One.
overview: ClickHouse develops an open-source, column-oriented database built for real-time analytics, and sells a managed cloud version.
bull_case: Fast growth, an open-source developer base and AI-driven demand could make ClickHouse a core database for real-time analytics.
bear_case: A roughly 60x revenue multiple assumes growth continues, while Snowflake, Databricks and cloud providers compete aggressively.
directory_notes: Revenue growth and path to IPO.
Competition from Snowflake, Databricks and hyperscalers.

intelligence.description: ClickHouse develops an open-source, column-oriented database built for real-time analytics, and sells a managed cloud version.
company: The ClickHouse database was first developed at Yandex and became an independent company in 2021. It is used for real-time analytics, observability and increasingly for AI workloads, and the company sells a managed cloud service alongside the open-source project.

In January 2026 ClickHouse raised a $400 million Series D led by Dragoneer at a $15 billion valuation, up from about $6.35 billion in its May 2025 Series C. By May 2026 it reported annualized revenue of $250 million, roughly triple the prior year, and more than 4,000 customers.
intelligence.why_it_matters: ClickHouse shows how AI and observability workloads are driving demand for new data infrastructure, and it is an IPO candidate that would be compared directly with Snowflake and Databricks.

changed.text: ClickHouse spins out as an independent company and raises its Series A and B.
A $350M Series C led by Khosla Ventures values it at about $6.35B.
A $400M Series D led by Dragoneer values it at $15B.
The company reports $250M in annualized revenue and says it is positioned for an IPO within a few years.

takeaways: Revenue roughly tripled in a year, which supports a steep valuation step-up.
The valuation is about 60 times annualized revenue, leaving little room for a slowdown.
AI companies are a growing customer group.
An open-source core helps adoption but can limit pricing power.
